oracle.independence: Written from RN's pinned sources, not from the probe: the members of ErrorUtils, the handler setUpErrorHandling registers, the error family ReactInstance defines with its arities and refusals, the flag default and the not-ready prefix are read from the files; RN's own error-guard, setUpErrorHandling, ExceptionsManager and NativeExceptionsManager are bundled by the same toolchain and run in V8 against a native module that records its calls, and what Hermes did with the same cases must be what V8 did; JsErrorHandler's pipeline before the runtime is ready is a model written from JsErrorHandler.cpp, whose anchors it finds in the source; every verdict of the probe is derived again from the report's raw observations.

catchSites.now: JsErrorPath::handle_fatal -> JsErrorHandler::handleError, fatal. RN's own scheduler wraps what Hermes throws as 'Non-js exception: <what>' (RuntimeScheduler_Modern.cpp:402; ReactInstance's runtime executor spells its wrap 'Non-JS exception: ', ReactInstance.cpp:107, and that is the spelling of the host's own catches).
catchSites.certifiedBy: fatal/An exception that escapes a task of RN's RuntimeScheduler ...

catchSites.site: pump(): the work queue (the host's runtime executor)
catchSites.now: JsErrorPath::handle_fatal; a Hermes JSError is recognised by its type name and reported as the JS error it is
catchSites.certifiedBy: none by a case of its own: native errors thrown by a work item are not reachable from JS; the scheduler site above is the one a JS error takes

catchSites.reactInstance: ReactInstance::loadScript, then the runtime executor's catch; setRuntimeReady after the evaluation (ReactInstance.cpp:287-299)
catchSites.now: load_bundle: handle_fatal while the runtime is not ready, bundle_evaluated() after a clean evaluation; mount stops the application without reporting twice
unchanged: slice F certifies callback exceptions against RN

catchSites.site: requestAnimationFrame callbacks, native animated and layout animation frames
catchSites.reactInstance: none: ReactInstance has no frame loop

limits: The timer, immediate, microtask and animation-frame catch sites keep the host's direct failure record; slice F measures callback exceptions against RN.

RN$hasHandledFatalException and RN$notifyOfFatalException are not installed: excluded by V2-D26 (the runtime keeps running after an uncaught error, with root-scoped recovery); with them ExceptionsManager.js reports only the first fatal exception. GF-07's error-cleanup slice owns any change.

Hermes' JSError and the host's have different type_info, so RN's own catch (jsi::JSError &) in JsErrorHandler and RuntimeScheduler does not match what Hermes throws: the scheduler reports 'Non-js exception: <what>', and an error raised while JsErrorHandler reports (a listener that throws) reaches the host's safety net instead of the next listener.
A soft exception is a log line, as on Android; iOS drops it without a redbox or a delegate. A fatal exception is a recorded failure and the application keeps running, where RN's release builds crash.
V2-D26's root-scoped unmount on an uncaught error belongs to GF-07's error-cleanup slice.
The headless desktop host only; no mobile export has run this bundle.

The lanes of this record are local. Hosted run 38481790977 (https://github.com/journey-studios/godot-fabric/actions/runs/38481790977), on head 26a3a908 (the slice before the review fixes), passed every job, native-suites-runtime with test:js-errors among them. The branch's later commits changed the evidence script, the oracle, the lane runner's provenance record, a named constant in native/js_error_path.cpp (the host built from it is byte-identical to the one built before it) and docs, so that run did not execute these exact bytes.
